note: Regions are in painting coordinates: x, y from 0 to 1 across and down, measured from the canvas edges; w, h are the region's full width and height as fractions of the painting's width and height; angle in degrees. Dwell is a minimum in seconds; the light waits at least as long as the speech.

paintings.title: Yellow painting
paintings.artist: So the wind comes, it's taking root, tension comes.

stops.say: The first thing is the yellow, the whole field of it, pushed outward from the middle as if a wind had just come through.
On the upper left the strokes are long and flat, all leaning the same way. This is where I feel the wind arriving.
Above the centre, a red curl hangs in a small clearing of white, like something the wind has just let go of.
Across to the right, two more red marks, thrown out like sparks.
Then my eye drops down a chain of dark green marks below the pink, and the movement starts to slow.
Lower, the marks grow heavy: mauve petals, a dark berry, curled green. They sag, as if they had weight.
Then a few dark red stems stand straight up. Whatever the wind carried here is taking root.
They reach down into the pale pink band where the paint has run, like roots into soft ground.
Back up in the middle, the pink figures pull in every direction at once. This is where the tension comes.
One arm stretches far out to the right while the rest of the group leans back to the left, and nothing settles between them.
I end on the raised hand at the top of the group, held open, still waiting.
I start in the top left corner, where faint pink lines cross under blue-green dots. It's the most measured part of the painting.
The dots march across the top in diagonal rows. Then the wind comes up from below, and the yellow begins to break them.
Here the yellow strokes wash right over the dots, as if the pattern were being blown apart.
A gray-blue cloud drifts among the dots, soft and blurred, like breath on glass.
On the right, the dots hold on in a narrow column running down the side.
It ends in a solid teal stripe along the edge, the pattern settling into one fixed band, rooted to the side.
On the far left, lower down, a matching strip of teal. Two posts set into the painting, holding it in place.
In the middle, the diamonds reach down deepest, almost touching the bright centre.
Right under them, orange strokes push up at an angle. The grid presses down, the bloom pushes up, and the tension starts here.
Below, the pink marks are everything the grid is not, each one reaching its own way. I end in that pull between order and growth.
Let me follow the reds. The first is this curl near the top, dark against white, like a drop the wind is still carrying.
A second flick of the same red drifts lower and to the left.
Across to the right, two more, scattered like sparks thrown out from the middle.
Then the red thins into the pink crowd. The same colour, but multiplied, as if the sparks had landed together.
Lower down, a single dark red dot is tucked inside green, the densest red in the bottom half.
Then a line of crimson ticks with one round dot at the end, like seeds falling into a row.
They gather into tall stems standing upright. The red has come down and taken root.
Off to one side, a single red mark lies flat on the ground, as if it never took hold.
Beneath everything, the red runs into faint drips, pulled down into the ground.
But back in the centre, one long maroon stroke cuts hard across the bloom, the most decisive line in the painting. This is where the tension comes from.
Beside it, a burgundy blot and a curved stroke like a wing, still pulling the other way. I end here, with the red caught between falling and flying.
This time the wind comes from below: a wide white arc sweeps through the lower right, the biggest and softest movement in the painting.
Along the bottom, the pink drips lean and ripple to the right, like the hem of a cloth in a draught.
In the middle of the drips, a thin green line rises, barely there. The first root.
Above it, the stems turn dark red and stand straight, three or four together. It's taking root.
Higher, they break into small ticks and one round dot, as if they had begun to bud.
Then the growth opens into mauve petals and curled leaves, spreading sideways.
A dark green curl anchors the right of the cluster, heavy like a hook.
From it, a chain of green climbs up the right like a vine, and the pull upward begins.
At the top of the vine, the pink figures burst outward in every direction.
And just above them, the blue-green diamonds press down like a trellis. The growth pushes up, the pattern holds it back, and the tension stays.
This time I stay near the edges. Along the top, a gray-blue cloud drifts through the dots, and the air seems to move here first.
To the left, the yellow strokes are long and flat, all leaning one way, like grass bent by the wind.
Down the left side, a dark teal band runs straight, the first thing that doesn't move.
Beside it, a patch of gold looks gritty, almost like sand, rough enough to hold on to.
Below, the left side opens into thin pale yellow where the canvas almost shows through. It's quiet here, like open ground.
At the edge of that space, a round yellow swirl, like a rose drawn in one circling stroke, planted at the border.
Across in the far corner, a patch of deeper ochre, as if the yellow above had settled and sunk in.
Further up the right edge, another gritty ochre patch, a twin of the sand on the left.
And at the top right, the teal stripe answers the band on the left. They don't line up, and the whole painting seems stretched between them.
I come back to the middle. Seen from the edges, the pink marks are where all that stretching pulls tight.
This time I watch how the paint moves. On the upper left the strokes are fast and flat, laid in one direction. This is the paint as wind.
Near the top, thick white and yellow are flung on, each stroke landing on the last.
On the right, the white arc is laid in one long pass, soft and wide, like a gust.
At the bottom, the paint has been thinned until it runs down. Here it stops moving sideways and sinks in.
One swirl lower down is made in a single circling motion, thin enough that I can follow the brush around.
The gold patch at the left is grainy, almost sand, a heavier skin of paint.
At the right edge, another rough patch, with one small bead of paint standing out of it, like something that has set.
Moving in, the strokes get shorter and curl back on themselves, ochre and white folded tight.
Here a white stroke has been dragged so its ridges stand up, like a fingerprint pressed hard.
And over it all, the pink marks, drawn with a narrow brush, quick and tense: the painting's handwriting. I end on them.
Some marks in the middle keep turning into figures for me, and they move as if a wind had caught them.
At the far left, a few round pink blots, like a head turned away from the gust.
Next to it, a looping figure with its arms up, leaning back as if pushed by the wind.
A line of short pink dashes streams off to the right, like a ribbon in the air.
It ends in a long arm reaching out, tipped with gray-blue, the farthest the wind carries them.
Below them, a long maroon stroke slants down, like a body bending low.
Further down, a rounded mauve shape wrapped in green, a figure folded in on itself, close to the ground.
Under it, a soft mauve loop, like a dropped scarf. Here they are settling, taking root.
But back in the middle of the group, the marks crowd and overlap, darker, pressed close together.
Just under the reaching arm, a small dark green hook, like a hand turned down, holding back.
I end on the raised hand above them all, open and held still. The wind has passed, but the tension stays.
